title: Lesson Three: Mind Your Own Business
coreMove: Mind your business by keeping earned income useful, then directing surplus into assets you understand and own until the asset column can buy freedom and luxuries.

exampleSpecs.stakes: The visible product can distract from the asset that creates durable value.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Ray Kroc's 1974 MBA lesson to separate hamburgers from location control.

exampleSpecs.stakes: An appealing operation may hide whether ownership rests in the service or the property.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Keith Cunningham's car-wash example to inspect the real estate beneath operations.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A bigger salary can strengthen everyone except the owner's asset column.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Trace wages to employer value, taxes, bank mortgage claims, and personal assets.

exampleSpecs.audience: high earners using titles as wealth signals
exampleSpecs.stakes: A respected profession can mask the absence of owned income-producing assets.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Separate earned income through work from a business as an owned asset base.

exampleSpecs.audience: new investors tempted by unfamiliar deals
exampleSpecs.stakes: Buying what sounds sophisticated can turn the asset column into a liability trap.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Require understanding before an investment earns a place in the asset column.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers balancing reward and wealth building
exampleSpecs.stakes: A desired luxury can consume the capital that should build future cash flow.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Delay the luxury until asset income can pay without weakening the principal engine.
